title: Splitting probabilities for Brownian motion with diffusing boundaries: Application to polymer translocation
authors: Alexander K. Hartmann, Satya N. Majumdar, Alberto Rosso
abstract: We study the translocation of a polymer chain through a nanopore where the chain length fluctuates stochastically due to the polymerization-depolymerization processes at the chain ends. We map this process to an equivalent representation where the pore performs a stochastic random-walk-like process on a line in the presence of two diffusing sinks on either side of it with diffusion constants $D_1$ and $D_3$ respectively. The translocation process terminates when the pore hits either of the two outer diffusing sinks. In the case where the pore motion itself is diffusive with diffusion constant $D_2$, we compute exactly the splitting probability that the pore hits the left (right) sink before hitting the right (left) sink. We show that the splitting probability in the presence of mobile sinks is rather nontrivial compared to the classical case of immobile sinks (the latter corresponds to the case when the chain length is fixed). Furthermore, we also compute exactly the probability distribution of the translocation time and that of the chain length at the completion time of the translocation. We show that both distributions have power law tails with exponents that depend continuously on the diffusion constants $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_3$. We validate our analytical predictions via numerical simulations. We then present numerical results for the case when the pore performs a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst exponent $0<H<1$, while the sinks are still diffusive.
summary: This work analyzes polymer translocation through a nanopore where the pore size fluctuates stochastically. By mapping this to a three-walker Brownian motion problem, the authors derive exact results for the splitting probability and show that the time and size distributions decay according to power laws dependent on the boundary diffusion rates. The study extends these findings to non-Markovian dynamics using fractional Brownian motion.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stochastic process of polymer translocation through a nanopore when the chain length fluctuates due to polymerization/depolymerization at the ends.
main_result: The splitting probability, translocation time, and final chain length distributions exhibit power-law tails whose exponents depend continuously on the diffusion constants of the boundaries and the pore.
method: The complex process is mapped to an equivalent problem of three interacting Brownian walkers (a vicious walker problem) on a line, allowing for exact analytical computation in some cases.
model_or_system: The system models a polymer chain translocating through a pore, represented by three coupled Brownian walkers with diffusion constants D1, D2, and D3. The outer walkers represent diffusing boundaries due to stochastic chain end processes.
key_observables: Splitting probability (hitting one sink before the other), probability distribution of translocation time, and probability distribution of the chain length at completion.
important_parameters: Diffusion constants {D1, D2, D3}, the Hurst exponent H (for fractional Brownian motion), and the initial pore size L.
main_assumptions: The process is modeled by mapping it to three vicious Brownian walkers; the analysis is exact for the three-walker case but requires numerical methods for fractional Brownian motion.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the polymer translocation process, the equivalent lattice model, and the trajectories of the three interacting Brownian walkers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the general physical problem to mapping it onto a three-walker diffusion process. It first solves the exact splitting probability for the diffusing boundaries, then derives the power-law exponents for the time and size distributions, and finally extends the analysis to the non-Markovian case of fractional Brownian motion using numerical simulations.
why_interesting: The mathematical techniques used to solve the three-walker vicious walker problem with non-trivial boundary diffusion are highly relevant to open quantum systems where boundaries or reservoirs are fluctuating or non-Markovian.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
